provenance.note: Generated by drivers/survival on the pystatsval harness against a PyPI-installed pystatistics==4.2.4. The 4.2.4 change is the Apple Silicon (MPS) float32 GLM IRLS inner solve: it moves from a Cholesky of XtWX to a GATED MATRIX-FREE CONJUGATE GRADIENT on the operator H v = Xt(W(X v)) (squaring-free -- XtWX is never formed). The host float64 Newton-decrement acceptance gate is unchanged and remains the sole arbiter of acceptance. Effect on the benchmarks: MPS now CONVERGES across the entire flchain person-period sweep -- including quarterly and monthly, which failed loud (not-positive-definite float32 Cholesky) at 4.2.1/4.2.3. On a genuinely float32-infeasible design the gate still refuses loud, now recommending backend='cpu' (Apple Silicon has no float64, so there is no gpu_fp64 path on MPS). CUDA (Cholesky) and CPU paths are UNCHANGED -- their numbers match 4.2.3 exactly. Correctness vs R is unchanged (round-off). MPS rows produced on torch 2.12.1; the MPS solver convergence envelope is torch-version-sensitive, while the host float64 acceptance gate is the version-independent guarantee that a wrong call fails loud. Hosts: powerhouse (Apple Silicon, CPU fp64 + Metal/MPS fp32, R 4.5.2) and forge (NVIDIA CUDA, CPU fp64 + CUDA fp32/fp64).
provenance.baseline: Compare against reports/survival-v4.2.3.md. Correctness identical (round-off); CPU and CUDA numbers unchanged. The change is on MPS: at 4.2.3 the float32 inner solve was Cholesky, which broke down not-positive-definite at quarterly (blank/intermittent at monthly); 4.2.4's gated matrix-free CG converges across the whole flchain sweep (quarterly 0.88s, monthly 8.33s on this host). The MPS device-pivot and precision tables, blank/rejected at quarterly+monthly in 4.2.3, are now fully populated and accepted.

r.engine: R survival::survfit / survdiff / coxph; glm(binomial) for discrete-time

reference.name: R survival::survfit / survdiff / coxph
reference.what: The R survival package (Therneau): survfit() for Kaplan-Meier, survdiff() for the log-rank test, coxph() for proportional hazards. Discrete-time survival is validated against R glm(family=binomial) on the identical person-period design pystatistics builds internally — on both the small survival::lung design and the large real survival::flchain design.

studies.title: Correctness vs R survival — Powerhouse (CPU / fp64), per quantity
Discrete-time CPU vs R on real flchain (~83k person-period rows), per quantity
Wall-clock vs R on survival::lung — Powerhouse (CPU / fp64)
studies.note: Per-fit median over timed repeats. With the 4.2.0 O(n log n) Cox PH, all four procedures are within a small constant factor of R on the tiny lung dataset; the scaling studies below carry the asymptotic and at-scale claims.

studies.title: Cox PH CPU scaling vs R — Powerhouse (CPU / fp64)
studies.note: Synthetic proportional-hazards DGP. pystatistics Cox PH is O(n log n) (vectorized reverse-cumsum risk sets + a Fenwick-tree concordance), matching R's complexity: the pystatistics/R wall ratio is FLAT at ~1-2.6x across n=250..8000.

studies.title: Discrete-time GPU fit scaling — Powerhouse: CPU (fp64) vs MPS (fp32)
studies.note: Wall-clock of the binomial GLM fit on the person-period design (expansion excluded). As of 4.2.4 the MPS float32 inner solve is a gated matrix-free conjugate gradient (squaring-free); MPS now converges across the ENTIRE flchain sweep including quarterly (0.88s) and monthly (8.33s) -- both were blank (not-positive-definite float32 Cholesky breakdowns) at 4.2.3. The host float64 acceptance gate is unchanged; a genuinely float32-infeasible design still refuses loud -> backend='cpu'. CUDA (see the Forge studies) remains the fp64-capable path.

studies.title: Discrete-time float32 acceptance boundary — Powerhouse (MPS): accurate when accepted, fails loud when wrong
studies.note: Per bin granularity: with the 4.2.4 gated-CG inner solve the MPS float32 fit is accepted across the whole sweep -- including quarterly (coef_max_rel ~4e-5 vs CPU), which the 4.2.3 Cholesky path rejected with a not-positive-definite NumericalError. The host float64 Newton-decrement gate is unchanged, so an accepted fit is genuinely at the float32 tier; a float32-infeasible design would still fail loud (-> backend='cpu'). faithfulness_rel ~0 confirms the fit-isolated measurement reproduces the public discrete_time coefficients.

studies.title: Expansion vs fit vs end-to-end — Powerhouse (CPU): the GLM fit dominates
studies.note: The person-period expansion is a pure-Python double loop but a small fraction of end-to-end at scale (~1.7% at monthly); the GLM fit dominates. As of 4.2.2 the CPU fit itself meets/beats R at scale (monthly 58s vs R glm 71s).

studies.title: R glm(binomial) at scale on the flchain person-period design — Powerhouse
studies.note: R glm wall climbs into the minutes at ~1M person-period rows (monthly ~71s). As of 4.2.2 the pystatistics CPU fit beats R there (58s); the CUDA gpu_fp64 path does it in ~4s.

studies.title: Discrete-time GPU fit scaling — Forge: CPU (fp64) vs CUDA gpu_fp64 (exact)
studies.note: The robust large-scale path: CUDA gpu_fp64 is exact (~1e-13, see the precision study) and accepted at every granularity including monthly -- ~9.5x faster than the same-host CPU fp64 fit (monthly 38s -> 4.0s). Speedup is smaller than 4.2.1 because the CPU baseline itself got faster (Core-QR, 4.2.2).

studies.title: Discrete-time GPU fit scaling — Forge: CPU (fp64) vs CUDA (fp32)
studies.note: CUDA float32 now converges across the WHOLE sweep including monthly (2.1s, ~18x over CPU) -- at 4.2.1 monthly float32 was the borderline reject; the 4.2.3 decrement-stop fix resolved it. Exact fits at every scale: use gpu_fp64 (above).

studies.title: Discrete-time GPU precision — Forge (CUDA): fp32 holds through quarterly, fp64 exact throughout
studies.note: CUDA float32 (backend='gpu') is accepted and accurate to ~1e-5 vs CPU across the sweep; CUDA gpu_fp64 is exact (~1e-13) at every granularity. CUDA is unchanged at 4.2.4 (the gated-CG change is MPS-only); the exact gpu_fp64 path remains CUDA's alone, as Apple Silicon has no float64.

record_fields.max_abs: max absolute difference between pystatistics and R over a quantity's elements
record_fields.max_rel: max relative difference between pystatistics and R over a quantity's elements (correctness headline)
record_fields.n_elements: number of scalar elements compared for that quantity (1 for scalars, vector length otherwise)
record_fields.speedup_vs_r: R wall-clock / pystatistics wall-clock on the same fit (>1 means pystatistics is faster)
record_fields.ratio_pystat_over_r: pystatistics wall-clock / R wall-clock at a given n (flat across n once both are O(n log n))
record_fields.peak_mem_mb: peak memory during the fit (GPU allocator high-water mark; process RSS delta on CPU)
record_fields.coef_max_rel: max relative difference of the float32 GPU covariate coefficients vs the CPU fp64 fit (float32 tier ~1e-5 when accepted)
record_fields.forced_max_rel: RIGOR R9: max relative error of the REJECTED float32 fit if forced (large -> the fit is genuinely wrong -> the rejection is a correct fail-loud)
record_fields.faithfulness_rel: max relative difference between regression.fit on the reconstructed person-period design and the public discrete_time coefficients (~0 -> the fit-isolated measurement is faithful)
record_fields.expansion_frac_of_e2e: person-period expansion time / end-to-end discrete_time time (small at scale -> the GLM fit dominates)
